_about: Demo tour of the rule-relative e-graph. Sources: verification/catalogue/pages/egraphs.md (its sources: list is the backbone; its Scope section states the exhaustive search and the one rewrite per round), verification/library/vox_egraph_rule_handle.md, the header comments of the vox_egraph_* files, research/mastery-20260927/demos-algorithms.md section 3.7; every claim re-checked against the code at 8479634adc.
title: Rule-relative e-graphs
summary: `Vox_egraph_rule_handle` is an e-graph for a small typed expression language whose answers are relative to the caller's rewrite rules: `Equal` comes with an erased derivation from those rules, and `Fixed_point` means that the returned graph is closed under the rules and congruence. The tour reads the interface, the specification of derivations and closure, a client and a rejected one, then the proof-carrying union-find and the saturation loop.

The rule search is exhaustive and does no e-matching: it enumerates every assignment of node ids to a rule's variables and every root, and each saturation round applies at most one rewrite. The [catalogue page](demo:egraphs) states the claim, the limits and the trusted base.

stops.title: The interface: query and saturate
stops.from: type equality = Equal | Not_proved | Invalid_input | Node_limit
stops.text: The graph `t` is abstract and `@ unique`: each operation consumes it and returns it in an unboxed record. `model` and `rules`, above, are ghost observations, so the contracts speak about a `Q.graph`, nodes and a class label per id, that exists only for the checker. `query` answers `Equal` only with a ghost `E.evidence` that is valid for the rules and whose two ends are exactly `left` and `right`; `Not_proved` carries no information, so a `query` that always says `Not_proved` meets the contract. `saturate` answers `Fixed_point` only when `Fixed.fixed` holds of the returned model, and `Rebuild_limit` and `Round_limit` carry no information. `create`, `admit`, `query` and `saturate` are not declared total, and their contracts hold on normal return.

stops.title: Derivations from the caller's rules
stops.text: An `evidence` is an `[@@inductive]` proof tree: `Refl`, `Sym`, `Trans`, one congruence step per constructor with children, and `Rule (i, rule, subst)`, one instance of rule `i`; `endpoints`, above, computes the two expressions it relates. `valid` checks every step: `Trans` only when the middle expressions are syntactically equal, congruence only at the right sorts, and `Rule` only when `rule` is exactly the `i`-th rule of the list and `subst` is well sorted. That last check is what ties an `Equal` answer to the caller's rules. The rules need not agree with the evaluator `L.eval`; [`Vox_egraph_interpret_wrapping.sound`](src:verification/library/vox_egraph_interpret_wrapping.mli) turns a valid derivation into equal evaluations only given a proof that every rule instance preserves evaluation.

stops.title: What a fixed point means
stops.text: Closure is stated per rule and per assignment. An assignment gives each rule variable a node id, or a negative id for no node; `binding_valid` requires the nodes to have the variables' sorts, and `closed_roots` says that at every root below `count`, if the left side matches, so does the right side. [`Vox_egraph_quantifier.closed_bindings`](src:verification/library/vox_egraph_quantifier.mli) ranges over all `(count + 1)^n` assignments of a rule with `n` variables, `closed_rules` asks it of every rule, and [`Vox_egraph_fixedpoint_spec.fixed`](src:verification/library/vox_egraph_fixedpoint_spec.ml) adds congruence closure: nodes with the same constructor and children in the same classes share a class. The specification quantifies over the same space that the search enumerates, so a search that completes without a change is a proof of closure. It states closure only; nothing says that classes are merged only when a rule or congruence requires it.

stops.title: A client: from Equal to equal evaluations
stops.text: `interpreted_query` creates a graph from `input_rules`, admits both expressions, saturates with 20 rounds, 20 rebuild passes per round and 100,000 units of search fuel, and queries. When the answer is `Equal`, the ghost `proof` field holds a derivation, and `Interpret.sound` turns it into `L.eval left env === L.eval right env` given `interpretation`, a ghost total function proving that both sides of every valid rule instance evaluate equally in `env`. The saturation status is ignored, which is sound because `query`'s contract does not depend on it. [`egraph_boundary.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/egraph_boundary.ml) compiles this client again with only the thirteen public specification and interface files visible.

stops.title: A rejected client: a limit is not a fixed point
stops.from: (* A saturation that stops at a limit does not establish a fixed point. *)
stops.text: A client that saturates with zero rounds and then claims `F.fixed` of the result is rejected, because `Round_limit` promises nothing. The same expect test rejects two other public programs: forging a `Vox_egraph_rule_handle.t` from `()`, since the type is abstract, and creating a graph from a rule whose sides have different sorts, which fails at the refinement `R.valid rs` of `create`. [`egraph_rule_rejected.ml`](src:testsuite/tests/vox/egraph_rule_rejected.ml) rejects two derivations: `foreign_rule` uses a rule that is not in the (empty) rule list, and `wrong_endpoint` chains `0 = 0` and `1 = 1` with `Trans`.

stops.title: Inside: the handle and its ghost model
stops.text: Behind the interface, a handle is the engine `H.t` (the hash-cons table and the store), the rules and a ghost `model`, refined by the engine's invariant, `R.valid rules`, and the equations `rules === store.semantic.rules` and `model === P.view store`. So `model` and `rules` in the interface are field reads, and every operation re-establishes the refinement when it rebuilds the handle. The hash-cons table is the flat hash table's implementation (`Vox_table_implementation.Make`), and the invariant ties its ghost ownership token to the table's state. `egraph_rule_public.ml` checks that in native code the handle has two runtime fields, with `model` erased.

stops.title: The key invariant: a union-find with proof edges
stops.text: At run time this is `union`, a parent array in which every id's parent is at most the id, so `root` terminates by recursion on the id; there is no path compression and no union by rank. The ghost fields record each id's origin expression and a derivation on its parent edge, and `valid` requires through `S.valid_edges` that each edge's derivation is valid for the rules and leads from the id's origin to its parent's. `merge`, below, takes a ghost derivation between the origins of the two roots and stores it on the losing root, so no merge happens without evidence. `same_evidence` chains edges into a derivation between any two ids of a class, which is where `query` and `same_class` get their proofs.

stops.title: The saturation loop: one rewrite per round
stops.from: fun state rules rounds rebuild_passes fuel ->
stops.text: One round is one call of `saturate`: `H.rebuild` restores congruence with passes that compare every pair of nodes, and `Rules.scan` then searches the rules once. The scan returns `Changed` at the first rule application that merges two classes or adds a node, so each round applies at most one rewrite, and a `Changed` scan starts the next round. A `Stable` scan means the store did not change and every rule is closed on it; together with the congruence closure from the rebuild (`CP.closed`), `F.fixed_def` gives the contract's `Fixed.fixed`, and the loop returns `Fixed_point`. Search fuel carries over between rounds, and rebuild passes are allowed anew in each round.

stops.title: The exhaustive rule search
stops.from: fun state rules index rule bindings count fuel ->
stops.text: The search is exhaustive and does no e-matching. For each rule, `rule` below enumerates every assignment of ids (or -1) to the rule's variables with `Vox_egraph_assignments.enumerate`, `cases` walks the assignments, and `roots`, shown here, tries `W.matched_rule` with every id from `count - 1` down to 0 as the root, so one search tries up to (count + 1)^n × count candidates for a rule with n variables. `matched_rule` either admits the right side and merges it with the root, justified by an erased derivation ending in a `Rule` step, or changes nothing, and any change returns `Changed` at once. When nothing changes, the ghost calls accumulate `C.closed_roots` for each assignment, and `Equiv.closed_rule` turns them into `closed_rule` from the specification. Each case, root attempt and enumeration step costs one unit of fuel; matching within one attempt is not charged.

stops.title: Emitted code and the trusted declarations
stops.text: `egraph_boundary.ml` compiles five runtime modules with `-dlambda`, and this program checks that none of them applies a function from the five listed proof modules; it is a text search of the emitted Lambda for direct calls. The same test regenerates [`vox_egraph_rule_handle.spec.json`](src:verification/library/vox_egraph_rule_handle.spec.json), the exact text of every top-level declaration in the thirteen files a reader must trust, and fails if it differs. Beyond those files and the checker, the e-graph trusts what the flat hash table trusts, the `Vox_iarray` externals `get` and `set`, and `Iarray.length` and `Iarray.Refined.get`. The node, sort and union-find arrays are immutable arrays updated by copying, so adding a node or merging two classes copies 512-element arrays.
